Gut microbiota of breast cancer patients with paclitaxel-induced neuropathy

16S rRNA V3-V4 re-analysis of E-MTAB-13423 (Zhong et al. 2023)

2026-11-22

Study design

Feces of 60 breast cancer patients who completed paclitaxel treatment and of 20 healthy controls were sequenced (16S rRNA V3-V4) by Zhong et al. (2023), Blockade of CCR5 suppresses paclitaxel-induced peripheral neuropathic pain caused by increased deoxycholic acid, Cell Reports 42:113386. Neuropathy was graded with NCI-CTCAE v4.0 and EORTC QLQ-CIPN20: grade ≥ 2 is high PIPN, grade 1 is low PIPN. Data: ArrayExpress E-MTAB-13423, ENA ERP152473. The rat experiment of the same paper is re-analysed with the same pipeline in ptx_rats_emtab13426.

The authors deposited only a relative-abundance table of the 20 most abundant genera. This analysis starts from the raw reads and produces ASV counts, which allow count-based methods (Chao1, DESeq2, ANCOM-BC2, rarefaction).

  • Healthy control: healthy volunteers, one sample each.
  • Low PIPN / High PIPN: breast cancer patients after paclitaxel, one sample each, taken after treatment.

Comparisons (fold changes are the second group relative to the first):

  • Control vs low PIPN: Low PIPN vs Healthy control.
  • Control vs high PIPN: High PIPN vs Healthy control.
  • Low vs high PIPN: High PIPN vs Low PIPN.

groupsequencing runsamplespatients

Read with two caveats.

  1. Patients vs healthy controls is not a paclitaxel effect alone. The controls do not have cancer and did not receive chemotherapy (breast cancer regimens usually combine paclitaxel with other drugs). Low vs high PIPN, both groups of treated patients, is the comparison closest to the question of the paper.
  2. Cross-sectional design, one sample per person. There is no sample before treatment, and diet, age, BMI and other drugs are not available in ArrayExpress, so they cannot be adjusted for.

Pipeline

  1. download_fastq / download_silva: submitted FASTQ from ENA (R1 and R2 are separate ENA runs) and SILVA 138.2 (DADA2 format, Zenodo), md5-checked.
  2. sample_metadata: sample sheet (group, patient, ENA runs of R1 and R2) parsed from the ArrayExpress SDRF.
  3. cutadapt (scripts/amplicon/trim_primers.sh): removes the 338F/806R primers, trying both mate orientations and re-orienting the reads.
  4. quality_profiles / filter_trim: DADA2 quality profiles, then filterAndTrim.
  5. dada2_denoise: error models per sequencing run × orientation batch (monotonic loess fit for binned quality scores), sample inference, pair merging, chimera removal.
  6. assign_taxonomy: naive Bayesian classifier against SILVA 138.2, then exact-match species.
  7. align_asvs / build_tree: MAFFT + FastTree, midpoint-rooted tree for UniFrac.
  8. build_phyloseq: phyloseq object (counts, taxonomy, tree, metadata).
  9. analysis (scripts/amplicon/analysis.R): composition, alpha/beta diversity, PERMANOVA, DESeq2 + ANCOM-BC2, comparison with the authors' table.
  10. report (scripts/amplicon/report.py): this page.
ENA FASTQ ──► cutadapt (both mate orientations) ──► DADA2 filterAndTrim
          ──► DADA2 learnErrors/dada per run × orientation batch ──► mergePairs ──► removeBimeraDenovo
          ──► SILVA 138.2 assignTaxonomy + addSpecies
          ──► MAFFT + FastTree (midpoint-rooted) ──► phyloseq ──► statistics ──► this report

Input data

The input is 80 paired-end samples from ENA (79 analysed). Sample names, groups, patients and sequencing runs come from the ArrayExpress sample sheet (data/E-MTAB-13423.sdrf.txt); the full sheet is results/samples.tsv.

L14 is excluded from the analysis: the deposited R2 file (ZTPSN21GP644-L14_R2.fq.gz) is an exact copy of R1 (same md5), so the pairs cannot be merged. It is kept in the read tracking table.

Read processing

  • Mate orientation: R1 starts with the forward primer (338F) in all 79 samples. trim_primers.sh tries both orientations and re-orients the reads, so "fwd" reads always start after 338F. Both primers were found in 92.2–97.4% of pairs per sample.
  • Read lengths: reads are 2×250 bp (R1 cut to 241–244 bp by the provider), ~222/231 bp after primer removal. Truncation is set to 220/229 bp, which leaves ~20 bp of overlap on the ~429 bp amplicon.
  • Chimeras: 40% of merged reads were removed as chimeras. Between 14,776 and 99,429 non-chimeric pairs per sample remain (18–77% of the raw pairs).
p_track <- track %>% left_join(meta %>% select(sample = sample_id, group), by = "sample") %>%
  select(sample, group, raw, primers_found, filtered, merged, nonchim) %>%
  pivot_longer(raw:nonchim, names_to = "step", values_to = "reads") %>%
  mutate(step = factor(step, levels = c("raw", "primers_found", "filtered", "merged", "nonchim"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(step, reads, group = sample, colour = group)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.6) + geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  scale_group_colour + scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Read pairs")
save_plot(p_track, "read_tracking", 9, 4.5)

Quality profiles and error models

Aggregate quality profiles of the primer-trimmed reads were used to choose the truncation lengths. The read headers show an Illumina NovaSeq run (ENA lists MiSeq) with binned quality scores (Q 2, 11, 25 and 37 only). With so few quality values the default loess fit of the DADA2 error model is poorly constrained, so the fitted substitution rates were forced to be non-increasing with quality (error_function: loess_monotonic). The "swapped" batch in the error-model figure holds only the excluded sample L14 (its two files are the same R1 reads, so almost no pair carries both primers).

ASV table and filtering

DADA2 produced 15,754 ASVs. 2 non-bacterial (Archaea or unclassified kingdom) and 41 chloroplast/mitochondria ASVs were removed, leaving 15,711. 59.6% of the kept ASVs (97.7% of the reads) have a genus assignment. Libraries have 14,776–99,405 reads (median 39,603); for alpha diversity, Jaccard and unweighted UniFrac they are rarefied to 14,776 reads.

otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) otu <- t(otu)
p_rare <- rarecurve(otu, step = 500, tidy = TRUE) %>%
  left_join(meta, by = c(Site = "sample_id")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Sample, Species, group = Site, colour = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = depth, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_group_colour +
  labs(x = "Reads sampled", y = "Observed ASVs", caption = "Dashed line: rarefaction depth")
save_plot(p_rare, "rarefaction", 9, 4.5)

From analysis.R

Taxonomic composition

Group averages

plot_group_means <- function(df, title) {
  m <- df %>% group_by(group, taxon) %>% summarise(abundance = mean(abundance), .groups = "drop")
  # Stack positions are computed over all segments before hiding labels of small ones.
  labs_df <- m %>% arrange(group, desc(taxon)) %>%
    group_by(group) %>% mutate(y = cumsum(abundance) - abundance / 2) %>% ungroup() %>%
    filter(abundance >= 0.04)
  ggplot(m, aes(group, abundance, fill = taxon)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.65, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text(data = labs_df, aes(y = y, label = scales::percent(abundance, accuracy = 1)),
              colour = "white", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
    taxon_fill(levels(m$taxon)) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = group_labels) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean relative abundance", title = title) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
}
save_plot(plot_group_means(phylum_df, "Phylum") + plot_group_means(genus_df, "Genus (top 8)"),
          "composition_group_means", 12, 5.5)

Per sample

plot_per_sample <- function(df, title) {
  ggplot(df %>% mutate(Sample = factor(Sample, levels = sample_order)), aes(Sample, abundance, fill = taxon)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.9, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    facet_grid(~ group, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x",
               labeller = as_labeller(group_labels)) +
    taxon_fill(levels(df$taxon)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative abundance", title = title) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 8),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
}
save_plot(plot_per_sample(phylum_df, "Phylum") / plot_per_sample(genus_df, "Genus (top 8)"),
          "composition_per_sample", max(10, 3 + 0.12 * n_samples), 9)

From analysis.R

Main phyla and the Bacillota/Bacteroidota ratio

Each panel shows one phylum (or the log2 Bacillota/Bacteroidota ratio). Brackets show BH-adjusted Wilcoxon p-values: the rank-sum test; all comparisons are between independent samples.

phyla <- phylum_df %>% filter(!taxon %in% c("Other", "Unassigned")) %>%
  group_by(taxon) %>% filter(mean(abundance) >= 0.005) %>% ungroup() %>%
  transmute(sample = Sample, group, subject, facet = as.character(taxon), value = 100 * abundance)
fb <- phylum_df %>% filter(taxon %in% c("Bacillota", "Bacteroidota")) %>%
  select(Sample, group, subject, taxon, abundance) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = taxon, values_from = abundance) %>%
  transmute(sample = Sample, group, subject, facet = "log2(Bacillota / Bacteroidota)",
            value = log2(Bacillota / Bacteroidota))
phyla_d <- bind_rows(phyla, fb) %>%
  mutate(facet = factor(facet, levels = c(sort(unique(phyla$facet)), "log2(Bacillota / Bacteroidota)")))
phyla_stats <- phyla_d %>% group_by(facet) %>% group_modify(~ group_tests(.x)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(label = fmt_p(p_adj))
save_plot(group_boxplot(phyla_d, phyla_stats, ncol = 3, ylab = "Relative abundance (%) / log2 ratio"),
          "phyla_boxplots", 10, 7.5)

Alpha diversity

Samples are rarefied to 14,776 reads. Brackets show BH-adjusted Wilcoxon p-values (the rank-sum test; all comparisons are between independent samples).

alpha <- estimate_richness(ps_rare, measures = c("Observed", "Chao1", "Shannon", "InvSimpson")) %>%
  mutate(sample_id = sample_names(ps_rare)) %>%
  left_join(meta, by = "sample_id") %>%
  select(sample = sample_id, group, subject, Observed, Chao1, Shannon, InvSimpson) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Observed, Chao1, Shannon, InvSimpson), names_to = "facet", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(facet = factor(facet, levels = c("Observed", "Chao1", "Shannon", "InvSimpson")))
alpha_stats <- alpha %>% group_by(facet) %>% group_modify(~ group_tests(.x)) %>% ungroup() %>%

Beta diversity

Four distances:

  • Bray-Curtis: relative abundances.
  • Jaccard: presence/absence, rarefied.
  • Unweighted UniFrac: rarefied.
  • Weighted UniFrac: relative abundances.

PERMANOVA (adonis2, 9,999 permutations) is run for each comparison separately. betadisper tests whether groups differ in spread.

Ordination (PCoA)

Each point is a sample. Large outlined points are group centroids, and dashed ellipses are 68% normal-theory regions.

pcoa_plot <- function(d, name) {
  ord <- cmdscale(d, k = 2, eig = TRUE)
  var_expl <- 100 * ord$eig[1:2] / sum(ord$eig[ord$eig > 0])
  df <- data.frame(ord$points, sample_id = rownames(ord$points)) %>% left_join(meta, by = "sample_id")
  cent <- df %>% group_by(group) %>% summarise(X1 = mean(X1), X2 = mean(X2))
  st <- permanova %>% filter(distance == name) %>%
    mutate(txt = sprintf("%s: R² = %.2f, %s", sub(" \\(paired\\)", "", comparison), R2, fmt_p(p_adj)))
  ggplot(df, aes(X1, X2, colour = group)) +
    subject_lines(geom_path, "grey82") +
    stat_ellipse(level = 0.68, linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.9) +
    geom_point(data = cent, size = 6, shape = 21, fill = group_cols[as.character(cent$group)],
               colour = "white", stroke = 1.5) +
    scale_group_colour +
    labs(title = name, subtitle = paste(st$txt, collapse = "\n"),
         x = sprintf("PCoA1 (%.1f%%)", var_expl[1]), y = sprintf("PCoA2 (%.1f%%)", var_expl[2])) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"))
}
save_plot(wrap_plots(Map(pcoa_plot, dists, names(dists)), ncol = 2, guides = "collect") &
            theme(legend.position = "top"),
          "pcoa", 10, 10)

From analysis.R

Effect size across distances

PERMANOVA R² is the fraction of between-sample variation explained by the grouping. Asterisks mark comparisons where betadisper finds unequal spread (p < 0.05). In those cases part of the effect may reflect dispersion rather than a shift in location.

p_r2 <- permanova %>%
  mutate(label = sprintf("R² = %.2f\n%s%s", R2, fmt_p(p_adj), ifelse(dispersion_p < 0.05, " *", "")),
         comparison = factor(comparison, levels = names(comparisons)),
         distance = factor(distance, levels = rev(names(dists)))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(comparison, distance, fill = R2)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label, colour = R2 > 0.35), size = 3.3, lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#cde2fb", high = "#104281", limits = c(0, NA), name = "R²") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey15"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
save_plot(p_r2, "permanova_r2", 10, 3.8)

Distance from the control community

For every sample, this is the mean Bray-Curtis dissimilarity to the 20 healthy control samples (excluding itself). Values near 1 mean almost nothing is shared. Group means: Healthy control 0.69; High PIPN 0.81; Low PIPN 0.82.

bc <- as.matrix(dists[["Bray-Curtis"]])
ctrl_ids <- meta$sample_id[meta$group == ref_group]
d2c <- meta %>% rowwise() %>%
  mutate(value = mean(bc[sample_id, setdiff(ctrl_ids, sample_id)])) %>% ungroup() %>%
  transmute(sample = sample_id, group, subject, facet = "Bray-Curtis to controls", value)
d2c_stats <- d2c %>% group_by(facet) %>% group_modify(~ group_tests(.x)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(label = fmt_p(p_adj))
save_plot(group_boxplot(d2c, d2c_stats, ncol = 1, ylab = "Mean Bray-Curtis dissimilarity"),
          "distance_to_control", 6, 4.5)

From analysis.R

Differential abundance (genus level)

ASVs are agglomerated to genus. Unassigned genera are labelled "<lowest assigned rank> (unclassified)". Each comparison is fitted on its own subset, keeping genera present in at least 25% of that subset. Two methods are used:

  • DESeq2 (negative binomial, poscounts): ~ group.
  • ANCOM-BC2 (bias-corrected log-linear model): group.

Genera with BH q < 0.05 in both methods are treated as robust. Positive log2FC = higher in the second group of the comparison.

Volcano plots

Each point is a genus. The x axis is the DESeq2 fold change and the y axis its p-value. Colour shows which method(s) call the genus significant. The six most significant genera called by both methods are labelled in each panel.

p_volcano <- ggplot(da %>% filter(!is.na(p_deseq2)), aes(log2FC_deseq2, -log10(p_deseq2), colour = called_by)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, called_by == "not significant"), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, called_by != "not significant"), size = 2.4) +
  geom_text(data = ~ filter(.x, called_by == "both") %>% group_by(comparison) %>%
              slice_min(p_deseq2, n = 6) %>% ungroup(),
            aes(label = genus), size = 2.9, vjust = -0.8, colour = "grey15", check_overlap = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ comparison, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = called_cols, name = sprintf("Significant (q < %s) in", da_q)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.12)) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change (DESeq2); positive = higher in the second group",
       y = "-log10 p (DESeq2)")
save_plot(p_volcano, "volcano", 13, 6)

From analysis.R

Genera that differ between treatments

These panels show the relative abundance (log scale) of every genus called significant by both methods in at least one comparison. Brackets give the ANCOM-BC2 q-value for each comparison in which the genus was tested.

pseudo <- 1e-3  # percent; zeros are plotted at this floor
rob_d <- genus_rel %>% filter(genus %in% robust) %>%
  transmute(sample = sample_id, group, subject, facet = genus, value = log10(100 * abundance + pseudo))
rob_stats <- da %>% filter(genus %in% robust, !is.na(q_ancombc2)) %>%
  transmute(facet = genus, comparison = as.character(comparison),
            label = paste0(fmt_p(q_ancombc2, "q"), ifelse(called_by == "both", " *", "")))
# Order panels: largest ANCOM-BC2 fold change first.
ord <- da %>% filter(genus %in% robust) %>% group_by(genus) %>%
  summarise(k = max(abs(log2FC_ancombc2), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% arrange(desc(k)) %>% pull(genus)
rob_d$facet <- factor(rob_d$facet, levels = ord)
rob_stats$facet <- factor(rob_stats$facet, levels = ord)
n_rows <- ceiling(length(robust) / 5)
p_rob <- group_boxplot(rob_d, rob_stats, ncol = 5, ylab = "Relative abundance (%)") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = log10(c(0, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100) + pseudo),
                     labels = c("0", "0.01", "0.1", "1", "10", "100"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.22))) +
  labs(caption = "* significant in both DESeq2 and ANCOM-BC2. Zeros plotted at 0.001%.")
save_plot(p_rob, "robust_genera", 12, 1 + 2.6 * n_rows)

From analysis.R

Heatmap of the most abundant genera

The 30 most abundant genera, each row scaled across samples (z-score of log10 relative abundance). Blue marks below-average abundance for that genus and red above-average. Rows are clustered, and the bar on the left gives the phylum.

top30 <- genus_rel %>% group_by(genus) %>% summarise(m = mean(abundance)) %>%
  slice_max(m, n = 30) %>% pull(genus)
hm <- genus_rel %>% filter(genus %in% top30) %>%
  mutate(v = log10(abundance + 1e-5)) %>%
  group_by(genus) %>% mutate(z = (v - mean(v)) / sd(v)) %>% ungroup()
zmat <- hm %>% select(genus, sample_id, z) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = sample_id, values_from = z) %>%
  column_to_rownames("genus") %>% as.matrix()
row_order <- rownames(zmat)[hclust(dist(zmat), method = "average")$order]
hm <- hm %>% mutate(genus = factor(genus, levels = row_order),
                    sample_id = factor(sample_id, levels = sample_order),
                    z = pmax(pmin(z, 2.5), -2.5))
p_heat <- ggplot(hm, aes(sample_id, genus, fill = z)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(~ group, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x", labeller = as_labeller(group_labels)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2a78d6", mid = "#f0efec", high = "#e34948", midpoint = 0,
                       limits = c(-2.5, 2.5), name = "z-score") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
phy_df <- tibble(genus = factor(row_order, levels = row_order), phylum = genus_phylum[row_order])
top_phy <- names(sort(table(phy_df$phylum), decreasing = TRUE))
phy_df$phylum <- factor(ifelse(phy_df$phylum %in% top_phy[1:min(4, length(top_phy))],
                               phy_df$phylum, "Other"),
                        levels = c(top_phy[1:min(4, length(top_phy))], "Other"))
p_phy <- ggplot(phy_df, aes(1, genus, fill = phylum)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(c(taxon_cols[seq_len(nlevels(phy_df$phylum) - 1)], other_col),
                                      levels(phy_df$phylum)), name = "Phylum") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "left")

Consistency with the authors' processed table

The authors' genus table (Greengenes, relative abundance; data/genus.txt) is compared with this analysis for genera with the same name in both taxonomies. Unclassified groups and bracketed Greengenes names (e.g. [Ruminococcus], a Lachnospiraceae genus unrelated to SILVA Ruminococcus) are excluded, and SILVA suffixes are stripped before matching. 18 genera match, and their mean abundances correlate with Spearman rho = 0.79.

p_auth <- ggplot(mean_ab, aes(authors + 1e-5, ours + 1e-5)) +
  geom_abline(colour = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(colour = "#2a78d6", size = 2) +
  geom_text(data = slice_max(mean_ab, pmax(authors, ours), n = 10), aes(label = genus),
            size = 3, vjust = -0.8, colour = "grey25", check_overlap = TRUE) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::percent) + scale_y_log10(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = "Mean relative abundance, authors (Greengenes)",
       y = "Mean relative abundance, this analysis (SILVA)",
       caption = sprintf("%d genera matched; Spearman rho of means = %.2f; dashed line: identity",
                         nrow(mean_ab), rho_means))
save_plot(p_auth, "authors_comparison", 7, 4.5)

From analysis.R

Sample label check

Each sample here is correlated (Spearman, shared genera) with every sample of the authors' table.

32 of 79 samples best match the authors' sample with the same label (Healthy control 6 of 20; Low PIPN 14 of 29; High PIPN 12 of 30). The authors' table holds only the 20 most abundant genera (18 shared with SILVA), so single-sample profiles discriminate poorly between people. The same-label correlation is still high (mean rho 0.79, vs 0.83 for the best match), and 57 of 79 samples best match an authors' sample of the same group. There is no sign of swapped labels.

wide_a <- authors_long %>% pivot_wider(names_from = sample_id, values_from = authors, values_fill = 0)
wide_o <- ours_long %>% pivot_wider(names_from = sample_id, values_from = ours, values_fill = 0)
shared <- intersect(wide_a$genus, wide_o$genus)
A <- as.matrix(wide_a[match(shared, wide_a$genus), -1])
O <- as.matrix(wide_o[match(shared, wide_o$genus), -1])
cross <- cor(O, A, method = "spearman")
ord_o <- c(intersect(sample_order, rownames(cross)), setdiff(rownames(cross), sample_order))
ord_a <- c(intersect(sample_order, colnames(cross)), setdiff(colnames(cross), sample_order))
p_label <- as.data.frame(cross) %>% rownames_to_column("ours") %>%
  pivot_longer(-ours, names_to = "authors", values_to = "rho") %>%
  mutate(ours = factor(ours, levels = rev(ord_o)), authors = factor(authors, levels = ord_a)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(authors, ours, fill = rho)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f4f3ef", high = "#104281", name = "Spearman rho") +
  labs(x = "Authors' table", y = "This analysis (labels from SDRF / file names)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1,
                                   size = if (n_samples > 40) 6 else NULL),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = if (n_samples > 40) 6 else NULL),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
save_plot(p_label, "label_check", max(10, 3 + 0.12 * n_samples), max(6.5, 1.5 + 0.11 * n_samples))

Configuration

Show config.yaml
# 16S rRNA (V3-V4) amplicon pipeline for E-MTAB-13423 (feces of breast cancer patients after
# paclitaxel, with low or high peripheral neuropathy, and healthy controls).
# Paths are relative to the project folder (ptx_patients_emtab13423/). Large files live under $DATA;
# those paths may use environment variables, which the Snakefile expands.

# ArrayExpress sample sheet (one row per FASTQ file: R1 and R2 of each sample were deposited as two
# separate single-end ENA runs). Copied from the ArrayExpress download; also defines the groups.
sdrf: "data/E-MTAB-13423.sdrf.txt"

# Authors' processed genus table (relative abundance of the 20 most abundant genera, QIIME 1.8 /
# Greengenes; UTF-16 text), from ArrayExpress. Used only for a sanity-check comparison in the report.
authors_genus_table: "data/genus.txt"

# Raw reads downloaded from ENA (ERP152473), outside the repository.
fastq_dir: "$DATA/Microbiota/PTX Zhong/E-MTAB-13423 feces PTX patients/fastq"

# Primer-trimmed and filtered FASTQ (intermediate, large), outside the repository.
work_dir: "$DATA/Microbiota/PTX Zhong/E-MTAB-13423 feces PTX patients/work"

# SILVA 138.2 formatted for DADA2 (https://zenodo.org/records/14169026); shared with the rat project.
silva_dir: "$DATA/refdb/silva_138.2_dada2"
silva_trainset_url: "https://zenodo.org/records/14169026/files/silva_nr99_v138.2_toGenus_trainset.fa.gz"
silva_trainset_md5: "1764e2a36b4500ccb1c7d5261948a414"
silva_species_url: "https://zenodo.org/records/14169026/files/silva_v138.2_assignSpecies.fa.gz"
silva_species_md5: "62fd939bd1aa9832d2089847f9f0b87d"

# Primers (ArrayExpress protocol P-MTAB-137189; same as the rat study). scripts/trim_primers.sh
# tries both mate orientations, so "fwd" reads always start after 338F.
primer_fwd: "ACTCCTACGGGAGGCAGCA"   # 338F
primer_rev: "GGACTACHVGGGTWTCTAAT"  # 806R

# DADA2 filterAndTrim parameters (lengths after primer removal).
# The reads are 2x250 (R1 cut to 241-244 bp by the provider, R2 251 bp), i.e. ~222-225 / ~231 bp
# after primer removal. 220 + 229 = 449 bp leaves ~20 bp overlap on the ~429 bp amplicon
# (338F-806R without primers), as for the 2x250 run of the rat study.
trunc_len_fwd: 220
trunc_len_rev: 229
max_ee_fwd: 2
max_ee_rev: 2

# DADA2 error model. The read headers (A01403:...:HHCCLDRXY) show an Illumina NovaSeq run with
# binned quality scores (Q 2/11/25/37), although ENA lists MiSeq. "loess_monotonic" forces the
# fitted error rates to be non-increasing with quality; "loess" is the DADA2 default.
error_function: "loess_monotonic"

# Taxonomy: classify ASVs in chunks with fewer threads, so the run fits in ~15 GB RAM
# (15,754 ASVs; a single call on 8 threads was killed by the OOM killer).
taxonomy_chunk_size: 2000
taxonomy_threads: 4

# Seq-run labels for the report.
seq_run_labels:
  GP: "GP (NovaSeq 2x250)"

# Samples kept through denoising (they appear in results/read_tracking.tsv) but left out of the
# phyloseq object and every statistic, with the reason shown in the report.
exclude_samples:
  L14: "the deposited R2 file (ZTPSN21GP644-L14_R2.fq.gz) is an exact copy of R1 (same md5), so the pairs cannot be merged"

# Study design. Group keys and labels, in plotting order (the first group is the reference for
# "distance to control"). Comparisons: fold changes are second vs first group.
subject_column: "patient"
groups:
  Control: "Healthy control"
  Low_PIPN: "Low PIPN"
  High_PIPN: "High PIPN"
comparisons:
  - {name: "Control vs low PIPN", groups: [Control, Low_PIPN], paired: false}
  - {name: "Control vs high PIPN", groups: [Control, High_PIPN], paired: false}
  - {name: "Low vs high PIPN", groups: [Low_PIPN, High_PIPN], paired: false}

# Genera highlighted by Zhong et al. (2023) for the patients (regex on SILVA genus names):
# higher Clostridium, Dorea and Ruminococcus in high PIPN; Sutterella, Dialister and Ruminococcus
# in low PIPN; Bifidobacterium (Bifidobacteriaceae) in healthy controls.
paper_taxa: "Clostridium|Dorea|Ruminococcus|Sutterella|Dialister|Bifidobacterium"

# Statistics.
min_prevalence: 0.25   # genus kept for differential abundance if present in >= 25% of the compared samples
da_qvalue: 0.05        # BH q-value cutoff, DESeq2 and ANCOM-BC2
permutations: 9999     # PERMANOVA and betadisper

# Random seed for rarefaction, DADA2 and permutation tests.
seed: 2023
